structure: Part 18, Address book. Read address-book.fit.spec.js in full and opened and mined all 9 traces it produced, every action of each: (L) address-book--address-book-list-categories-pagination-and-filters.zip, 94 actions; (T) ...choose-an-address-type.zip, 47; (O) ...origin-or-consignor-an-address-entered-by-hand-with-its-uses.zip, 65; (D) ...destination-consignee-or-importer-a-uk-address-found-by-postcode.zip, 73; (B) ...branch-a-uk-address-found-by-postcode-with-the-branch-address-use.zip, 35; (R) ...transporter-hands-over-to-the-add-a-transporter-pages.zip, 25; (U) ...the-usage-step-is-only-reachable-with-an-address-pending.zip, 21; (V) address-book--an-address-book-entry-view-edit-and-save.zip, 67; (X) address-book--an-address-book-entry-delete-confirm-then-the-list-says-it-was-deleted.zip, 43. All 0 errors; validation shows as rendered error pages. Page inventory, in journey order: (1) address-book list /design-release-2.1/address-book with four category tabs (?category=origin-and-consignor default, destination-consignee-importer, transporter, branch), pagination (?page=2) and a collapsed Filter addresses disclosure holding Search and Type, plus success banners after add, edit and delete (L action 23, 33, 42, 51, 60, 75; O 46; V 48; X 24). (2) choose-an-address-type /address-book/add with its error state (T 16, 28). The type then routes: origin-and-consignor to (3) add-an-address manual entry /address-book/add/lookup with the full country list and its error state (O 16, 27); destination-consignee-importer and branch to (4) find-address /address-book/add/find-address with its error state (D 17, 28), then (5) select-an-address /address-book/add/find-address/select (D 41), then back to (3) prefilled with a UK-only country (D 54); branch via Enter address manually to (3) with the UK-only country and a single Branch address use (B 16); transporter hands over to /design-release-2.1/transporter/add Choose a transporter type (R 12), which another part owns and is claimed here only as the hand-over target. (6) /address-book/add/usage redirects to /address-book/add when no address is pending (U 7); its own page never rendered. Entry pages: (7) view /address-book/<slug> (V 13), (8) edit /address-book/<slug>/edit with its error state (V 25, 35), (9) delete confirmation /address-book/<slug>/delete (X 13). Network logs were read for every trace: only same-origin page GETs and form POSTs with 302 redirects, no lookup or data API call from the browser, and the list search fires no request. Every row and option value is prototype demo data. Not reached: Type filter, no-result searches, page 3, No, cancel, saving a found or branch address, view/edit/delete of non-origin entries, the usage page itself; these are gap claims.

The trace never uses the list's Type filter, so whether it filters on the client or by submitting the GET form, and what it shows, are not seen.
No trace shows a search that finds nothing, or the empty state of a category with no addresses.
No trace shows the last page of a category (page 3 of Origin and Consignor) or a Previous link being followed.
No trace shows format validation for the postcode, email address or phone number on the add or edit pages: no badly formed value was entered.
No trace shows the find-address errors for a badly formed postcode or a postcode with no addresses, or the select-an-address error for continuing without choosing an address.

No trace saves a Destination, Consignee or Importer address or a Branch address, so the save, the success banner and how those rows show in their list are not seen. The trace also never shows what happens when no use is ticked.
No trace views, edits or deletes a Destination, Consignee and Importer, a Transporter or a Branch entry, so their entry pages, including whether a transporter shows its approval number, are not seen.
No trace presses the edit page's Cancel button, so where it leads is not seen.
No trace uses the select-an-address page's 'Change postcode' or 'Enter address manually' links, so what they keep or clear is not seen.
